question: Should ClawHub adopt an advisory-first capability manifest as a supported public skill-metadata contract, and which boundary categories and verification expectations are authoritative in its first version?
rationale: The remaining work selects a durable public trust boundary and rollout policy; source changes cannot safely decide its schema, authority, legacy treatment, or enforcement posture.

options.title: Adopt a narrow advisory schema
options.body: Define a versioned manifest for the four proposed boundary categories, preserve legacy skills, and surface declared-versus-observed mismatches only for review.

options.title: Extend existing metadata incrementally
options.body: Add only declarations already supported by current registry metadata and defer broader execution/filesystem semantics until a shared ecosystem schema exists.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep current scanning and moderation signals without a public capability API until maintainers can sponsor the schema and verification model.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow advisory schema
recommendation.body: Define a versioned manifest for the four proposed boundary categories, preserve legacy skills, and surface declared-versus-observed mismatches only for review.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the closest merged manifest metadata surface and is the strongest available routing candidate for compatibility with it.
